transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-02
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (AstraNova Dir MLOps), Emily Jordan (Data Platform Lead), Sofia Martinez (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be partial): Align on POC milestones, confirm security checklist, agree benchmark metrics and timelines.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call, and then we'll run through the gates we usually use for these POCs.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Hi all, Raj here. We're excited to get this moving. We've had some internal talks about latency targets and cost buckets.
[00:20] Emily Jordan: Emily here, we run the data platform and will own the sample traces and tokenization.
[00:25] Sofia Martinez: Sofia — I'll be attending exec readouts, but day-to-day Raj and Emily will drive.
[00:35] Liam Ortega: Great. Quick agenda: 1) agree success criteria, 2) access plan and gating, 3) benchmark methodology, 4) timeline and milestones, 5) open Qs. I'll toss in our baseline scripts and what we measure.

[02:05] Raj: For success criteria we care about three pillars: p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, and output quality (safety + accuracy). For latency, we're aiming for p95 < 200ms for short chitchat flows, but for longer generative sequences maybe 300–400ms is acceptable — depends on seq length.
[02:40] Liam Ortega: Good note. For the POC we usually pick two traffic shapes: interactive (seq len avg ~40 tokens, target QPS 25–50) and batch/ingest (avg seq len ~512, QPS low). We'll run steady-state and spike tests. Our starter target for p95 is 150ms for the interactive path on a dedicated pool; we can demonstrate baseline hosted numbers as well.
[03:20] Emily: That 150ms sounds optimistic; what's the hardware you're assuming? We typically have CPU-side preprocessors and then GPU inference.
[03:30] Liam Ortega: The baseline will be on A100/RTX-class equivalent (Redwood Dedicated test pool). We'll annotate the exact instance type in the benchmark spreadsheet. Also we'll show results for a quantized variant so you can see cost tradeoffs.

[05:00] Maya Chen: Let's enumerate gates — we propose 4: Kickoff (today), Access & Baseline (week 1), Mid-point tuning & regression tests (week 3), Exec readout + Go/No-go (week 5). Does that cadence make sense?
[05:30] Raj: Week 5 for exec readout is reasonable. Our internal timeline: procurement sign-off by end of November ideally, so faster if possible.
[05:45] Sofia: We want clear pass/fail criteria for exec readout — not just 'looks good'.
[05:55] Maya Chen: Agreed. Example pass criteria: p95 latency below threshold for interactive path, accuracy metric within 2% of current baseline on eval set, and cost per 1M tokens <= agreed threshold. Also security checklist satisfied (SOC2 region, KMS keys present, VPC peering validated).

[08:10] Emily: About security, we need SSO (SAML) for the Redwood console, audit logs exported to our SIEM, and BYOK (KMS) for any customer keys. Can you support HSM-backed keys?
[08:35] Liam Ortega: Short answer: yes — Redwood Private supports HSM/KMS integrations. For the hosted POC we'll provide a private control-plane option and can enable KMS-wrapped keys. We'll share the runbook for SSO and VPC peering. Note: cert exchange for peering can take a few days on your side.

[11:00] Raj: Access timeline question — how long from our ACL approval to test cluster access?
[11:10] Liam Ortega: If all network bits are green, typically 3–5 business days to provision test pool and temporary credentials. If there's additional legal review for IP, might push longer.

[12:30] Maya Chen: For benchmarks, Liam, can you explain the scripts and the metrics you capture?
[12:40] Liam Ortega: Sure. We'll run two harnesses: 1) latency harness — warmup then steady-state with synthetic traffic shaped by your token distribution; capture p50/p90/p95/p99, tail behavior, token/s. 2) throughput sweep — increasing concurrent requests to find saturation. We'll also capture cost estimates (GPU-hours, tokens) and model quality metrics: BLEU/ROUGE-like for structured tasks and a pass/fail accuracy for your canonical evals. We'll commit the harness scripts to a shared repo.
[13:55] Emily: We need the ability to replay real traces — will the harness accept captured traces?
[14:05] Liam Ortega: Yes, replay is supported. Please scrub PII before sharing. The harness can replay arrival patterns, token lengths, and seeded randomness to ensure repeatability.

[20:00] Raj: On workload sizing: we expect 40 sustained concurrent interactive users initially, spiking to 120 during peak. Token distribution: median 35, 90th 220, occasional long sessions to 2k tokens.
[20:25] Liam Ortega: That helps. We'll size the dedicated pool accordingly — probably starting with 2 GPUs for the interactive workload and a separate batch lane for long sequences. We'll show cost scaling if you move to 4 GPUs.

[25:00] Emily: How do you handle KV cache and long context? We rely on context windows up to 8k currently.
[25:15] Liam Ortega: Our runtime supports KVM/kv cache (note: transcription may show KV cahce) and dynamic attention kernels up to 32k in some model families. For the POC we'll test your 8k flows specifically and measure overhead and memory pressure.

[30:30] Maya Chen: Can we quickly align on the exec readout content? What does AstraNova want to see?
[30:40] Sofia Martinez: At a minimum: 1) an executive one-slide TL;DR with pass/fail, cost delta, and recommended next step; 2) a technical appendix with latency/throughput plots, and 3) security/compliance attestation. Also a short demo of the model responding to our top 3 prompts.
[31:10] Maya Chen: We'll prepare that template. For pass/fail, we will include binary flags per gate and an overall recommendation.

[34:00] Raj: Any concerns about data residency? We process EU customer data and need logs to remain in eu-west; is that supported?
[34:12] Liam Ortega: We support region pinning for Dedicated and Private. For hosted tests we can provision a eu-west test cluster if required; note pricing varies. We'll note region in the benchmark spreadsheet.

[36:50] Emily: On the benchmark metrics, can you include cost per inference and cost per 1M tokens in the sheet? We'll need that for our FinOps.
[37:00] Liam Ortega: Yes — the spreadsheet has fields for GPU-hours, tokens generated, and a calculated cost line using Redwood pricing assumptions. We can also show a projected monthly run rate at different QPS.

[40:15] Maya Chen: A few logistics: we'll need a single Slack channel for the POC, access to your engineering repo with samples, and a contact list for escalation.
[40:30] Raj: Agreed. We'll create a channel after we get the access checklist.

[42:00] Emily: Regarding prompt sets for quality evaluation, we have three buckets: 1) short Q&A (chatty), 2) structured extraction, 3) long summarization. We'll share 30 examples per bucket.
[42:20] Liam Ortega: Perfect. For quality we will run automatic scoring where possible + a small human review for summarization. We'll include human eval guidance for the exec readout.

[50:00] Maya Chen: Risks: procurement delays; network peering delays; model mismatch on accuracy. Mitigations: early legal review, early cert exchange, and a canary test with a small sample to validate model quality within week 1.
[50:25] Raj: Can we add an optional stress test that simulates a sudden 10x burst?
[50:30] Liam Ortega: Yes — we can run a burst scenario and show graceful degradation and fallback to a cheaper model variant if needed. We'll include fallback handoff latency in the results.

[58:00] Sofia Martinez: One more question: are logs immutable and exportable? We need tamper-evident audit trails for compliance.
[58:10] Liam Ortega: Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM, and we support write-once storage patterns for longer retention in Private deployments. We'll provide the retention matrix in the security runbook.

[65:00] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps and owners — we'll post the checklist and spreadsheet, Liam will provision a baseline cluster, Raj/Emily to share prompts and traces. Mid-point demo in week 3, exec readout week 5.

[66:20] Raj: Sounds good. I'll coordinate internal stakeholders and aim to have artifacts by 2025-10-08.
[66:40] Emily: We'll scrub PII and deliver the traces.

[68:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the mid-point and exec readout.

End of transcript. Some auto-caption errors present (model names, KV cache spelled a few ways).
